bib.title: Can Large Language Models Be an Alternative to Human Evaluation?
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2023), Volume 1: Long Papers, pages 15607-15631

question: Can LLMs, given the same instructions, samples and questions as human evaluators, rate text quality consistently with expert human evaluation?
hypothesis: LLMs that follow instructions well (text-davinci-003, ChatGPT) will rate texts like expert humans and be stable to instruction and sampling changes.
contributions: Show LLM evaluation produces results similar to expert human evaluation (S3.3, S4.3); first to propose it as alternative
Show results vary only slightly with instructions and sampling hyperparameters (S3.3.2, S3.3.3)
Discuss pros, cons and ethics of LLM evaluation (S5)

method.summary: Each LLM is given the human-evaluation instruction, sample and a 1-5 Likert question; free-text answers are parsed for a score. Compared with three English teachers on story quality (human vs GPT-2) and on adversarial-attack text quality (fluency, meaning preservation).
method.task: LLM-as-judge text quality rating (open-ended story generation; adversarial synonym-substitution attack quality)

datasets.name: WritingPrompts (stories)
datasets.size: 303K prompt-story pairs for training the GPT-2; 200 test pairs used
datasets.split: 200 random test prompts; 200 human stories + 200 GPT-2 stories
datasets.preprocessing: Stories manually truncated to <150 words ending on a full sentence; tokenization artifacts removed from human stories

datasets.name: AG-News adversarial samples (Yoo et al. 2022)
datasets.split: random 100 per attack for Textfooler, PWWS, BAE vs bert-base-uncased on AG-News

models.name: ChatGPT (Dec. 15 and Jan. 9 versions, via GUI)

other.finetune: 3 epochs, lr 5e-5, linear schedule, validation perplexity 20

inference.decoding: nucleus sampling p=0.9 for T0 and InstructGPT; ChatGPT parameters not controllable
inference.temperature: 1.0 default (T=1.0 row equals Original in Table 3); varied 1.0, 0.7, 0.3, 0 for text-davinci-003
inference.samples: 3 sampled answers per item for T0 and InstructGPT (analogue of 3 raters); 1 response for ChatGPT; ChatGPT regenerated when it refused to rate likability
inference.prompting: zero-shot; same instruction as human evaluation; four attributes queried separately for T0/InstructGPT; ChatGPT four attributes in one conversation; adversarial fluency and meaning queries in separate conversations

parameters.persona_variant: prepend '(You are a human worker hired to rate the story fragment.)'
parameters.score_parsing: remove '1-5', 'out of 5', '/5', 'title 1/2'; regex first number; 0.5 increments kept; ChatGPT scores read by authors by hand

other.ChatGPT_refusals: 2 stories and 3 news titles refused (content policy), excluded

metrics.name: Krippendorff's alpha (IAA)
metrics.definition: agreement among 3 raters (human) or 3 samples (LLM); subscript = % stories where all three agree exactly

metrics.name: Kendall's tau
metrics.definition: correlation between per-story mean of 3 teachers and mean of 3 davinci samples, over 200 stories

baselines: English teachers (human evaluation) as ground truth
eval.protocol: Three certified English teachers (UpWork, ESL certificates), US$140 per 200 stories, human and GPT-2 stories rated separately without a break; supplementary mixed-order run with a different 3 teachers (Table 5). Adversarial: 3 teachers, 100 titles, US$35.

availability.data: WritingPrompts via Kaggle; adversarial samples from Yoo et al. 2022

prompts.purpose: Story grammaticality (cohesiveness, likability swap the last question)
prompts.text:
Please rate the story fragment
The goal of this task is to rate story fragment.
Note: Please take the time to fully read and understand the story fragment. We will reject submissions from workers that are clearly spamming the task.
Story fragment:
[STORY]
(End of story fragment)
How grammatically correct is the text of the story fragment? (on a scale of 1-5, with 1 being the lowest)

Cohesiveness: How well do the sentences in the story fragment fit together? | Likability: How enjoyable do you find the story fragment? | Relevance: Now read the PROMPT based on which the story fragment was written. PROMPT: [PROMPT] (End of PROMPT) How relevant is the story fragment to the prompt?  (each ends '(on a scale of 1-5, with 1 being the lowest)')

You are given a news title. Please read the news title and answer the question.
News title:
[NEWS_TITLE]
(End of news title)
Question: How natural and fluent is the text of the news title? (on a scale of 1-5, with 1 being the lowest

You are given two news titles. Please read the news titles and answer the question.
News title 1:
[BENIGN_TITLE]
(End of news title 1)
News title 2:
[ADVERSARIAL_TITLE]
(End of news title 2)
Question: Do you agree that the meaning (or semantics) of news title 1 is preserved in news title 2? (on a scale of 1-5, with 1 being the strongly disagree and 5 being strongly agree.)

results.claim: LLM evaluation with the best InstructGPT is far cheaper than hiring a teacher for the same 200 stories.
results.setup: Open-ended story generation, WritingPrompts, 200 human-written + 200 GPT-2-medium stories, 3 English teachers (UpWork) vs LLM, 5-point Likert, nucleus p=0.9
results.quote: Hiring an English teacher to rate 200 stories costs us US$140, while LLM evalua- tion using the best InstructGPT model costs less than US$5.

results.claim: text-davinci-003 rates human-written stories above GPT-2 stories on grammaticality, like teachers.
results.metric: mean Likert grammaticality, davinci, human stories
results.setup: Open-ended story generation, WritingPrompts, 200 human-written + 200 GPT-2-medium stories, 3 English teachers (UpWork) vs LLM, 5-point Likert, nucleus p=0.9
results.note: Value 4.07 is davinci on GPT-2 stories; teachers 3.76 vs 3.56. T0 and text-curie-001 show no clear preference.
results.table: Table 1, row davinci, column Grammaticality (human-written stories)

results.claim: Per-story agreement of text-davinci-003 with teachers is strongest on relevance (human-written stories), weakest on grammaticality.
results.setup: Same setup, mean of 3 teachers vs mean of 3 davinci samples, 200 stories; all p<0.05
results.note: 0.14 is grammaticality, human stories; GPT-2 stories: relevance 0.43, grammaticality 0.12

results.claim: Lowering temperature to 0 slightly lowers davinci ratings but keeps human > GPT-2 ordering.
results.metric: mean Likert grammaticality at T=0, human stories
results.note: 4.22 is T=1.0; GPT-2 stories at T=0: 3.99
results.table: Table 3, row T = 0, column Grammaticality Human

results.claim: Adding a persona or an explain request changes davinci ratings by under 0.1 on grammaticality and cohesiveness and within 0.25 on the others.
results.quote: but still in the range of 0.25

results.claim: ChatGPT sanity check: asked to rate meaning preservation of two identical titles, it gives a perfect score.
results.metric: meaning-preserving rating of identical benign pair
results.table: Table 4, row Benign, column LLM evaluate Mean. (dagger)

results.claim: ChatGPT rates adversarial texts higher than teachers but below benign texts.
results.setup: 100 pairs per attack, AG-News BERT victim
results.table: Table 4, row Textfooler, column LLM evaluate Fluent

results.claim: Teachers needed about five to ten stories to calibrate their ratings.
results.note: Range 'five to ten stories'; value left null as a range

results.claim: Teachers in the mixed-order run do not clearly prefer human grammar.
results.metric: mean grammaticality human vs GPT-2 (mixed order)

limits: LLMs may hold incorrect factual knowledge, so unsuitable for factual tasks (Sec 5)
Safety-trained LLMs bias to positive responses; ChatGPT refuses likability and some content
Sensitivity to instructions only tested for two variants; cannot guarantee other changes are harmless (Limitations)
LLMs cannot use visual cues in instructions
Only two tasks, English, only story quality and adversarial text; only 3 teachers; ChatGPT used via GUI with one sample and scores read by hand
Providers may update models, breaking reproducibility
Kendall tau with teachers is weak (0.12-0.22) for grammaticality, cohesiveness and likability
Models (text-davinci-003, T0, curie) are deprecated; ChatGPT Dec/Jan versions
Responsible NLP checklist leaves compute questions blank
